plain.li: [clear] Clear, still night, and every footstep in the place carried straight to my bed.
[old] Up twice for my own reasons and three times for everyone else's.
[lowmood] Woke at every sound. I was half waiting for one anyway.
[good] {OTHER_nameDef} and I went at it in the yard until we were both too winded to swing. Then we sat down, and it was over.
[good] Got a black eye off {OTHER_nameDef}. Gave one back. The air's cleaner between us than it's been for weeks.
[good] Fought {OTHER_nameDef} today, fair and square. Afterward {OTHER_nameDef} helped me up.
[bad] {OTHER_nameDef} hit me first. I don't remember what I said to deserve it, which worries me.
[bad] Fought with {OTHER_nameDef} in front of the others. I'm more ashamed of that than of the bruise.
[bad] {OTHER_nameDef} and I fought, and nobody won. Two sore faces and the same argument.
[bad] My hand still hurts from {OTHER_nameDef}'s jaw. It was a stupid fight about a stupid thing.

warm.li: Hit {OTHER_nameDef}. I've never hit anyone I liked before. I'll make it right.

blunt.li: {OTHER_nameDef} had it coming. Still sore, though.

cheerful.li: Wrestled {OTHER_nameDef} into the mud! I lost, but it was a magnificent loss.

gloomy.li: Fought {OTHER_nameDef}. We're all so tired that it was always going to be someone.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} drops the left hand when tired. I'll remember that.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} did the voice again, the one that's supposed to be mine.
{OTHER_nameDef} has a new nickname for me. It's caught on, which is the worst part.
{OTHER_nameDef} told the table about my mistake at the workbench. It gets funnier every time, apparently.
[newcomer] {OTHER_nameDef} keeps making jokes about where I came from. I'm still too new to answer back.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} teases everyone, I know. I'd still like a day off from it.

blunt.li: {OTHER_nameDef} thinks I'm the joke. I'm not.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} made fun of my hat, so I wore it to supper on purpose. Twice the hat.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} was only joking. I've been told so four times today.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} needs an audience for the jokes. I'll see that there isn't one.

plain.li: Somebody told me what {OTHER_nameDef} said about me. I wish they hadn't.
{OTHER_nameDef} has been talking. The cook knew before I did.
Walked in on {OTHER_nameDef} telling a story about me. It was mostly wrong, and I didn't correct it.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} has been talking about me. I'd rather {OTHER_pronoun} had just asked me.

blunt.li: {OTHER_nameDef} has a big mouth. I'll stop feeding it.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} has been spreading stories about me, and they're more exciting than my real life.

gloomy.li: They've all heard it by now. I can tell by the way they look at me at supper.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} can't keep a thing to {OTHER_objective}self. That cuts both ways.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} borrowed my needle a week ago. My shirt is still waiting for it.
Asked {OTHER_nameDef} about my cup. Apparently it's been lent on to someone else.
My whetstone is somewhere in {OTHER_nameDef}'s things. My knife is getting duller by the day.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} forgot to give back my hat again. I'll put my name inside it this time.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} still has my spoon, so I've been eating soup with a ladle. I recommend it.

gloomy.li: Lend something here and it's gone. I should have learned that by now.

cold.li: I've stopped lending {OTHER_nameDef} anything I'd mind losing, which is everything.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} left the room when I came in. I gave it a moment, then I went in after.
Three days now and {OTHER_nameDef} hasn't said a word to me that wasn't about work.
{OTHER_nameDef} laughed at something across the table and stopped when I looked over.

warm.li: Left a bowl of berries on {OTHER_nameDef}'s bench. No note. We'll see.

blunt.li: {OTHER_nameDef} can talk to me when {OTHER_pronoun}'s ready. I'm not chasing.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} is still not talking to me, so I've started narrating my day out loud nearby.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} won't speak to me, and the others have started picking sides.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef}'s silence tells me more than {OTHER_possessive} talk ever did.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I went over who stands where when the next fight comes. We agreed, mostly.
[mage] Showed {OTHER_nameDef} how I shape a working. {OTHER_nameDef} asked better questions than most students.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} asked how I was holding up after the last fight, and waited for the real answer.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I worked out a signal for the next fight. It's a sort of whistle, and I'm very proud of it.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I planned for the worst. It's what we're good at.

plain.li: [spring] Spring, and "{WISH}" is done. I whistled the whole way back from the fields.
[spring] They saw to "{WISH}" between the planting and the rain. I don't know how they found the time.
[spring] New shoots in the fields, and "{WISH}" done. Good week.
[summer] Long hot day, and at the end of it, "{WISH}". I sat with it until the light went.
[summer] They did it in the middle of the busiest season. I noticed.
[summer] "{WISH}" is done. I've been in a good mood all day, and the heat hasn't spoiled it.
[fall] The council got "{WISH}" done before the cold. Good timing, and I said so.
[fall] Harvest's in and so is "{WISH}". A good season, whatever else happens.
[fall] With everyone busy in the fields, someone still found time for "{WISH}".
[clear] Clear evening, and I walked out to look at it twice before bed.
[highmood] Good day all round, and then they came through on "{WISH}" on top of it.
[trusting] I knew they'd see to "{WISH}". It's nice to be right about people.

warm.li: I found the people who did the work and thanked them by name.
They said yes to "{WISH}". I want to give something back, and I'm thinking about what.

blunt.li: Got it. Didn't even have to ask twice.
They did "{WISH}". Took a while. Done now.

cheerful.li: "{WISH}" happened. I've told everyone, and the animals too.
They said yes! I hugged the doorframe.

gloomy.li: They came through on "{WISH}". I'll enjoy it before something comes along to take it.
Got what I asked for. I don't quite know what to do with being happy.

cold.li: They argued about it, I hear. I'll remember who was on which side.
"{WISH}" delivered, close to when they said. Noted in their favor.

plain.li: [spring] They came through the new crops. Half the field is trampled flat.
[spring] Fought in the mud. I lost a boot in it and haven't found it.
[spring] They came on the first warm day. I'd been looking forward to that day.
[summer] Fighting in the heat. Afterward we drank the water barrel dry.
[summer] They came at dusk, out of the long grass. We'll cut it back tomorrow.
[summer] Sweat and smoke all afternoon. I can still taste both.
[fall] They came for the harvest. They didn't get it.
[fall] Fought among the fallen leaves. By the end I couldn't tell blood from mud.
[fall] They came before the frost, as if they knew our stores were full.
[winter] They came over the frozen ground. We held.
[winter] Fought in the cold until my fingers wouldn't close. Someone had to pry the weapon out of my hand.
[winter] Short day, long fight. It was dark before we'd counted everyone.

warm.li: We carried the hurt ones in between us, two to a stretcher.

cheerful.li: The stew survived, and so did I!

gloomy.li: We won today. I don't feel like it.

cold.li: We held, but the east side was slow. I'll say so tomorrow.

plain.li: The promise ran out today, and not one of them came to say sorry.
They promised "{WISH}". I told the others they'd keep it. Now I have to eat that.
[doubtful] I didn't fully believe them, and I was still disappointed.
[winter] A promise broken in the dead of winter. It feels colder than it is.

warm.li: Maybe they couldn't. I'd still have liked to hear it from them.
I'll forgive it. I'll remember it too, but I'll forgive it.

blunt.li: A promise means something. Apparently not here.
They broke it. I won't ask again.

cheerful.li: Promise broken. Still, I've got my health and half a loaf of bread.
They forgot their promise. I'll remind them, cheerfully, every single day.

gloomy.li: They promised. I should have known what that's worth here.
I counted the days down to nothing. Next time I won't count.

cold.li: A broken promise. I've written down the date, and the names.
The council's word has a price. I've just learned what it is.

plain.li: They told me "{WISH}" was coming, and it came. That's all I ever wanted from them.
Promise kept. Next time they speak at a meeting, I'll listen properly.
[trusting] I said they'd keep it, and they did. I told the doubters at supper.

warm.li: They kept their word. I'd have carried water for them all week for it.

cheerful.li: They kept their promise, so I'm keeping mine: an extra slice of pie for everyone who helped.

gloomy.li: They kept it. I'm ashamed of how sure I was that they wouldn't.

plain.li: Not a yes, not a no: "{WISH}" just ran out of days.
I only noticed it had lapsed because I'd been counting the days.
[trusting] I'm sure they meant to get to it. They didn't.

warm.li: It didn't happen. I'll mention it more gently next time, or more often.

cheerful.li: Missed my chance this time. I'll ask again when the weather's better, and louder.

gloomy.li: Another thing I wanted, gone past. I've stopped keeping a list.

cold.li: Lapsed. I'll take my next request to whoever actually gets things done.

plain.li: They said no to "{WISH}". At least they said something.
Refused. I nodded the whole time, then kicked a bucket on the way out.
[trusting] The council said no. I suppose they know something I don't.

warm.li: They turned me down. I'll ask what would change their minds, once I'm calmer.

cheerful.li: They said no! Well, now I know where I stand, and it's right here, still cheerful.

gloomy.li: A no. I'd prepared for it, and it still landed.

cold.li: Refused. They'll find it harder to ask me for things now.

plain.li: Folded {OTHER_nameDef}'s blanket and didn't know where to put it.
The others keep looking at me as if I might break. I might.
I keep remembering the last ordinary thing {OTHER_nameDef} said to me. It was about the weather.

warm.li: Told the youngest a story about {OTHER_nameDef} tonight, so it gets remembered.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} had the loudest laugh at the table. I keep waiting to hear it.

gloomy.li: The colony feels smaller without {OTHER_nameDef}, and colder.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef}'s tools are still where {OTHER_pronoun} left them. I'll move them when it's useful to. Not yet.

plain.li: Got tired of asking and took care of it myself. Should have done it weeks ago.
Fixed it myself this afternoon, with a borrowed hammer and some swearing.
[old] At my age you learn not to wait. Sorted it out before supper.

warm.li: Fixed it myself, and fixed the same thing for the one next door while I was at it.
Saw to it on my own. I didn't want to bother the council with something so small.

blunt.li: Wasn't going to wait on anyone else. So I did it.

cheerful.li: Did it myself and it turned out better than I'd hoped. I'm a genius, occasionally.
Sorted it out with my own two hands and a lot of muttering.

gloomy.li: Did it myself. Easier than waiting for a council that wasn't coming.
Fixed it. I didn't do it for thanks, which is just as well.

cold.li: Handled it without the council. I'll keep doing that where I can.
Done myself, done right, done by noon.
